_about: The plain definitions behind every (i) on the site, and the /terms/ page. One sentence or two, for someone who has never used a radio. tools/shell.py writes them into the pages; edit them here, then run it.

pass.name: Pass
pass.plain: The few minutes a satellite spends above a station's horizon. Each pass happens once. If it is missed, its data is gone.

ground-station.name: Ground station
ground-station.plain: A receiver on the ground (an antenna, a radio and a small computer) that listens to satellites as they fly over.

element-set.name: Element set
element-set.plain: The published numbers that describe a satellite's orbit, used to predict where it will be. They age: a week-old set predicts less accurately than yesterday's.

elevation.name: Elevation
elevation.plain: How high a satellite climbs above the horizon during a pass, in degrees, from 0 at the horizon to 90 straight overhead. Higher usually means a cleaner signal, but it is one clue among several.

predicted-yield.name: Predicted yield
predicted-yield.plain: Meridian's estimate of how likely a pass is to return usable data. It answers 'will this work?', not just 'will the satellite be visible?'.

schedule.name: Schedule
schedule.plain: Which station listens to which pass, decided for all stations at once, so the most promising passes are covered and no station is asked to be in two places.

lrpt.name: LRPT
lrpt.plain: The digital picture signal sent by the Meteor-M weather satellites on 137 MHz. It is what Meridian's first station is built to receive.

decode.name: Decode
decode.plain: Turning a raw radio recording into the satellite's actual data. For a weather satellite, that means an image.

heartbeat.name: Heartbeat
heartbeat.plain: A short message a station sends regularly to say what it is doing. It is how Meridian tells a station that was listening apart from one that was switched off.

simulated.name: Simulated (SIM)
simulated.plain: Produced by Meridian's simulator, a set of practice stations that behave like real ones, rather than by a real antenna. Always marked SIM, and never mixed with real results.

reception-confidence.name: Reception confidence
reception-confidence.plain: How sure Meridian is that a reception's data is usable, as a percentage. It is checked against what really happened: of the passes marked 80%, about 80 in 100 should turn out good.

loss-cause.name: Loss cause
loss-cause.plain: When a pass returns nothing useful, Meridian's best explanation: view blocked, radio interference, clock wrong, receiver off or satellite silent. When the evidence does not point anywhere, it says 'undetermined' instead of guessing.

health-warning.name: Health warning
health-warning.plain: An early notice that a station is slowly getting worse, sent to its owner before it fails outright.

area.name: Area
area.plain: A place someone wants to keep an eye on, such as a farm, a forest or a town, followed over time with public satellite data.

msp.name: MSP
msp.plain: Meridian Station Protocol: the open, published rules a station follows to join the network. Any station that follows them can take part, whatever software it runs.

evidence-dataset.name: Evidence dataset
evidence-dataset.plain: A sealed, downloadable copy of every pass and its result, with the settings used, so anyone can check Meridian's figures for themselves.
